general_notes: Candidates fall into five recurring types per state: (1) in-app dark-vignette presentation of the painting (3-4 per state, near-identical to each other); (2) the original painting inset with a flat brown border (closest to target); (3) a heavily blurred full-frame copy; (4) a zoomed-in vignette crop that cuts off legs/feet; (5) a 3D/vector re-creation that is a different rendering. Differences among the vignette variants (spark density, smoke) are small and some scores between them are uncertain at the viewed resolution. The depleted target itself contains a grey rectangular patch at lower right; the vignette variants remove it, which I scored as a presentation difference rather than a defect. In motion, frame-to-frame differences are subtle at this resolution; I could not detect any warping or tearing artefacts, but small artefacts could be missed. None of the sequences show body motion (bob, sway, slump), only flame/ember variation.
